subject: Cloud Computing
title: Serverless Limits and Tradeoffs
description: Learn Serverless Limits and Tradeoffs in one minute.

hook.text: Serverless sounds perfect until you hit a 15-minute timeout, a 250 MB package limit, or a cold start.

buildup.text: Every serverless platform imposes constraints: max memory, execution time, payload size, concurrency.

discovery.text: These limits exist because the provider must share resources fairly among millions of functions.

twist.text: Some workloads don't fit: long-running processes, WebSocket connections, or heavy stateful computation.

climax.text: Serverless is a tool, not a religion. Use it where it fits. Use servers where it doesn't.

punchline.text: Serverless isn't for everything. Knowing when to stop is the skill.

quiz.question: Why do serverless platforms have strict execution limits?
options: Resources must be shared fairly among millions of concurrent functions
Serverless hardware is physically weaker than regular servers
Cloud providers want to force customers to upgrade to IaaS

details.summary: Serverless has constraints including execution time limits, memory caps, cold start latency, limited local storage, and reduced observability. These trade-offs make serverless unsuitable for long-running processes, stateful workloads, or latency-critical applications.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing serverless for unsuitable workloads leads to frustration and workarounds. Understanding its limits ensures you apply it where it genuinely excels.
takeaways: Execution time limits typically cap at 15 minutes
Cold starts add latency for infrequently invoked functions
Limited local storage and no persistent state between calls

faq.question: What workloads should not use serverless?
faq.answer: Long-running batch jobs exceeding timeout limits, workloads needing persistent local state, GPU-intensive computing, applications requiring websocket connections, and latency-critical services that cannot tolerate cold starts are poor fits for serverless.

faq.question: How can cold start latency be reduced?
faq.answer: Use provisioned concurrency to keep instances warm, minimize deployment package size, choose lightweight runtimes like Node.js or Python, and avoid VPC attachments when unnecessary. Some providers also offer snap-start features that pre-initialize functions.
